problem.text: The wrapper loaded tokenizer.json without explicitly disabling backend truncation. Encoding helpers then consumed the backend's returned IDs directly.

reasoning.text: Calling no_truncation() once during construction establishes the policy on the shared backend before vocabulary probes and subsequent encoding, rather than modifying each encoding call.

impact.text: For tokenizers loaded with truncation enabled, the intended effect is to preserve input tokens instead of silently shortening backend encodings. This does not itself provide model-context-length enforcement.

source_notes.text: The earlier tokenizer entry describes absence-safe BOS/EOS lookup; those guards remain present and are not modified by this change.

Issue #7 reports an undefined native symbol, while issue #15 reports incoherent low-bpw output and discusses quantization regularization. Neither discussion identifies tokenizer truncation as its cause.

limitations: No backend tokenization or complete initialization was executed; no affected tokenizer artifact or reproduced truncated input was supplied.
A standard-library scalar computation would not validate this external-backend state change, so no substitute numerical test was performed.

chapters.title: Disable backend truncation at tokenizer initialization

claims.text: Tokenizer.__init__ now calls self.tokenizer.no_truncation() after loading the backend and auxiliary JSON dictionaries, before the BPE space/newline probes. The call is unconditional and adds no wrapper option.

encode_special, encode_unspecial and num_tokens all use this same backend. Public encode still adds optional BOS/EOS tokens and left-pads list inputs to the longest encoded sequence; these operations are unchanged.

Removing backend shortening favors complete encodings over honoring a serialized truncation policy. Previously capped inputs may consequently produce longer tensors and require length handling by callers.

annotation.summary: Disable truncation on the shared tokenizer backend during initialization, without changing wrapper encoding or padding logic.
